messages:
Leah R: hit a weird failure after following the quickstart on an offline laptop. installer finished but `redwoodctl login` fails with cert verify.
Tom B: paste exact error?
Leah R: `Error: POST \"https://auth.internal.redwood.local/oauth/device\": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`
Ishan: ah installer logged something about using a cached endpoint during discovery fallback? did it print a warning?
Leah R: yes: 'Discovery failed, using cached control plane: https://auth.internal.redwood.local' — I assumed that was fine.
Kai L: that's the old behavior. interactive installs accidentally merge a cached internal endpoint into ~/.redwood/config.yaml if discovery times out. not ideal for laptops.
Tom B: workaround: edit ~/.redwood/config.yaml and set profile.endpoint to https://auth.redwood.ai then `redwoodctl login --method device`.
Leah R: I tried that but the laptop is air-gapped from corp CA so TLS still fails when the CLI tries internal host for something else.
Kai L: you can force an endpoint override with env var: `REDWOODCTL_FORCE_ENDPOINT=https://auth.redwood.ai redwoodctl login --profile default --method device`. that'll avoid the cached host.
Ishan: also `redwoodctl local-serve --profile default --trust-ca /path/to/corp.pem` is handy for test VMs that only have the corp CA locally.
Leah R: forcing endpoint worked, device flow completed. thanks.
DevEx Bot: created DEVEX-1507: "installer: do not merge cached internal endpoints on interactive installs; add explicit --preserve-endpoints flag"
Tom B: suggest installer shows a clearer message when discovery fails: "Could not reach discovery; refusing to silently use cached internal endpoint — run with --preserve-endpoints to keep cached endpoints"
Ishan: I'll open a PR and add an e2e that simulates discovery timeout to ensure installer prompts unless `--preserve-endpoints` passed.
Leah R: adding a note to onboarding FAQ about offline workshop setups and the env var workaround.
Kai L: thanks — small DX win for folks doing demos.
